checks.what: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan gains Darfur from british-africa, 1 Jan 1930. The page says 'the British conquered Darfur in 1916' and 'The kingdom was incorporated into the Anglo-Egyptian Condominium in 1917' (no month), so a 1930 start is a window-limited fix. The region, Sudan plus South Sudan, is 9,221 cells (about 2.33 M km2). The gain takes only cells british-africa holds, so exactly 1,086 cells move, as vassal of united-kingdom like the rest of the Sudan. Trial: the Sudan holds 9,190 cells in 1930-33 and 9,221 from 1934; the 1934 snap now adds only the 31 french-africa border cells. No other year changes.

Manchukuo gains Rehe from the Republic, March 1933. The page supports the date: 'Rehe Province got annexed on the 4 March 1933'; 'from the Chinese warlord Zhang Xueliang'; Chaoyang and Kailu on 25 Feb, Chifeng from 2 Mar, Chengde on 4 Mar. The region resolves to 1,008 cells (about 255,000 km2) at 38.8-47.0N, 115.1-123.6E. That is larger than the whole province (179,982 km2, infobox of the Rehe Province page), part of which is already inside Manchukuo's 1932 shape. About 201 cells in the west are northern Chahar (the land Mengjiang's 1936 founding takes from Manchukuo), and the Battle of Rehe page does not name it. The Mengjiang page supports that strip: 'In a series of actions, starting in 1933, the armies of Manchukuo and Japan occupied Chahar and in 1936 proclaimed itself the independent Mongol Military Government'. The rest is within the project's factor-of-two tolerance. Trial: the cells are the Republic's in 1932 and Manchukuo's (vassal of Japan) in 1933-35. In 1936 Mengjiang takes 201 of them, and in 1937-39 the provisional government takes about 200 by the size rule (a separate problem, listed below). Before the patch, 789-1,008 cells were grey.
checks.fix: Note amended: names the Chahar strip and the oversize against the 179,982 km2 infobox area, and quotes the Mengjiang page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mengjiang) for the Chahar occupation from 1933. Region unchanged, because no page gives Rehe's outline.
